script.opening: “Hello doctor. Since the stroke clinic changed my tablets I feel terrible — dizzy, aching all over, tired. I read the leaflet and the blood pressure one says dizziness. I want to stop the new ones, honestly.”

facts.text: “Light-headed, like I might faint, when I stand up — getting out of bed, getting up from the sofa. It passes if I sit down.” Not spinning. Started a few days after the changes. Nearly fell once holding the worktop; no injury, no blackout.
No weakness, numbness, face drooping, speech or vision problems since the TIA. No headache.
No chest pain, no palpitations, no breathlessness.
“Both thighs and shoulders ache, like after gardening.” Can climb stairs and lift the kettle — no real weakness. Urine normal colour. Began about a week after starting the cholesterol tablet.
Bruises a bit more easily. No black stools, no blood in urine, no nosebleeds.
Some bloating, bowels normal, no weight loss. Tired. Drinks “not much — I don’t want to keep going to the toilet at work”.

facts.topic: Home BP (only if the doctor asks you to measure it)
facts.text: You have Kofi’s machine. Sitting, after resting: “104 over 62, pulse 76.” After standing for a minute (only if asked to stand and repeat): “86 over 54… I feel a bit swimmy.” Sit down if told.

facts.topic: How she takes her tablets (only if asked exactly how she takes them, or to read the boxes)
facts.text: “I have my pill organiser from before, with the amlodipine and the losartan 50. Then the chemist gave me the new boxes — the losartan 100, the clopidogrel, the statin — so I take those as well, every morning.” Not aware this means losartan twice.

facts.topic: Family and fears (if asked what worries her)
facts.text: “My mother had a stroke at 60. She couldn’t speak or walk after. I can’t end up like that.” Then: “But these tablets are making me ill.”
Ward clerk at the hospital — off this week. Husband Kofi back tomorrow. Two adult sons. Does not smoke, no alcohol. Church on Sundays. Cannot drive for a month.

Be fed up but reasonable. Reveal the tablet doubling only if asked how you take your tablets. If the doctor explains that the double dose may cause the dizziness, be relieved. If offered ramipril, refuse — it gave you a cough. Agree to keep the clopidogrel and statin if the doctor explains why and has a plan for the aches.

ice.ideas: “The new tablets are poisoning me — the leaflet says dizziness.”
ice.concerns: HIDDEN AGENDA — She has been taking the old losartan 50 mg from her pill organiser as well as the new 100 mg, without realising. Openly: frightened of a stroke like her mother’s, and frightened of the tablets.
ice.expectations: Permission to stop the new tablets.

cues: “The leaflet says dizziness.” — she has a theory worth exploring.
“My mother had a stroke at 60.” — the fear that can make her keep going with treatment.
“I take those as well.” — the dosing error.

checkpoints.text: Characterises the dizziness as postural light-headedness, screens for recurrent TIA, cardiac symptoms and bleeding on clopidogrel
Asks about muscle symptoms in detail (site, weakness, dark urine) and timing in relation to atorvastatin
Uses the home BP monitor during the call to show postural hypotension, and asks exactly how she takes each tablet — finding the duplicated losartan
Stops the duplicate losartan 50 mg, keeps losartan 100 mg, advises slow position changes and adequate fluids, and arranges a nurse lying/standing BP and bloods (U&E, CK, LFT, FBC, TSH) tomorrow
Advises continuing clopidogrel and atorvastatin, explains their benefit after TIA, and sets out the statin muscle-symptom plan (CK > 5 × ULN — stop; otherwise review, rechallenge or switch)
Arranges a pharmacist medicines review and a single updated organiser; offers a fit note; gives FAST and 999 safety-netting and a follow-up date
Acknowledges her experience and her fear of stroke, uses shared decision-making, and changes one thing at a time with her agreement

worked.txt: “Can you read me each box you take from, and tell me which ones go in the pill organiser?”
“You’ve got Kofi’s machine — could you sit for a minute and take a reading? Then stand up, hold on to something steady, and take it again after a minute.”
“Your pressure drops when you stand — that’s the light-headedness. You’ve been taking 150 of losartan instead of 100. Let’s stop the old 50s today; that alone may fix it.”
“The clopidogrel and the statin are the two tablets that most reduce the chance of the stroke you’re worried about. Let’s check your muscle blood test before deciding anything about the statin.”

f.learning: When a patient blames new medicines, take the symptom seriously and look for a mechanism before stopping anything. Ask exactly how each tablet is taken — duplicated doses after a change (old stock in a pill organiser plus a new box) are common. Remote consultations can still gather data: a validated home monitor gives seated and standing readings (a systolic fall of 20 mmHg or more, or a diastolic fall of 10 or more, is postural hypotension). After a TIA, antiplatelet therapy and high-intensity statin are the key preventive treatments; the BP target is usually below 130/80, but postural symptoms and falls take priority. An ARB dose increase needs U&E (creatinine, potassium) in 1–2 weeks. For statin muscle symptoms: check CK; if more than 5 × the upper limit of normal, stop; otherwise consider a pause and rechallenge, a lower dose or another statin. Change one medicine at a time so the cause can be identified. A Black African or Caribbean family origin is relevant to antihypertensive choice (ARB rather than ACE inhibitor) — and here she also has a documented ACE-inhibitor cough. Car drivers must not drive for one month after a TIA.

knowledge.guideline: NICE NG128 Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management (2019, updated 2022) · NICE NG136 Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management (2019, updated 2023) · NICE NG238 Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification (2023) · NICE NG5 Medicines optimisation (2015) · DVLA Assessing fitness to drive (TIA: car drivers 1 month)
knowledge.summary: Find the postural drop and the double losartan; stop the duplicate, keep the clopidogrel and statin, check U&E and CK tomorrow, and safety-net for stroke.

points.t: Ask: spinning (vertigo), unsteadiness, or light-headedness on standing? Postural light-headedness points to hypotension. Measure seated then after 1 minute standing (and 3 minutes if possible). Falls risk matters more than tight targets.

Old stock, pill organisers and new boxes are a classic route to duplication after a dose change. Ask the patient to read every box. Fix with a single updated list, community pharmacist review (New Medicine Service) and, if helpful, a pharmacy-filled organiser.
Check U&E 1–2 weeks after starting or increasing an ARB: a creatinine rise above 30% or potassium above 6.0 needs action. Dehydration and overdosing increase risk.

Ask about weakness and dark urine. Check CK (not routinely if asymptomatic). CK over 5 × ULN — stop and recheck. Lower CK with tolerable symptoms — consider continuing, pausing and rechallenging, a lower dose, or switching (for example to rosuvastatin). Check TSH and vitamin D if symptoms persist.

Clopidogrel 75 mg long term (or per clinic plan); high-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) with a target of over 40% non-HDL reduction; BP below 130/80 when tolerated; lifestyle. Stopping these raises stroke risk.
Car drivers must not drive for 1 month after a TIA (no need to tell the DVLA if fully recovered). A fit note is reasonable while symptoms settle.

model.text: Hello, Mrs Mensah? It’s Dr Patel. I can see you were at the TIA clinic recently. Tell me how you’ve been since.
model.why: Uses the record, invites her story

model.text: Dizzy, achy, tired. The leaflet says the blood pressure one causes dizziness. I want to stop them.
That sounds miserable. Tell me more about the dizziness — is the room spinning, or do you feel faint? When does it happen?
Faint, when I stand up. It goes if I sit.
Any weakness, numbness, speech or vision problems since the TIA? Any chest pain, palpitations, black stools or unusual bleeding?
model.why: Recurrent TIA, cardiac and bleeding screen

model.text: No, none of that. A few more bruises.
And the aches — where, and is there any real weakness or dark urine?
Thighs and shoulders. No weakness. Urine’s normal.
Do you have a blood pressure machine at home? Could you take a reading sitting, then standing after a minute, holding on to something?
model.why: Remote examination with the patient’s own device

model.text: Sitting 104 over 62. Standing… 86 over 54. I feel swimmy.
Please sit down. Could you read me the boxes you take your tablets from, and what’s in your pill organiser?
Organiser has amlodipine and losartan 50. Then the new boxes — losartan 100, clopidogrel, the cholesterol one.

That explains a lot. You’re taking losartan twice — 150 instead of the 100 the clinic wanted — so your pressure drops when you stand. From tomorrow morning, take out the losartan 50 and keep the 100. Get up slowly and drink a bit more.
model.why: Clear explanation and a single change

model.text: Oh! I didn’t know. And the others?

I know your mum had a stroke — the clopidogrel and the cholesterol tablet are the two that most protect you from that. Aches can be from the statin, so I’ll check a muscle blood test tomorrow with your kidney tests. If it’s high, we stop it; if not, we have options like a different statin.
model.why: Links to her fear; statin pathway; bloods

model.text: Kofi’s back tomorrow — he can bring me.

The nurse will check your blood pressure lying and standing and take bloods tomorrow, and I’ll ask the pharmacist to sort one clear list. If your face drops, your arm goes weak or your speech goes — even briefly — call 999. What are you going to change tonight?
Take the losartan 50 out of the box, keep the others, get up slowly, see the nurse tomorrow — and 999 if I get stroke signs.

social.t: Reading the leaflet is a sign of engagement. Respecting her theory and testing it builds trust in the treatment she most needs.
Restricting drinks to avoid toilet trips at work worsens postural hypotension; address it practically.

legal.t: Car drivers: no driving for 1 month after a single TIA; may resume if no residual deficit — no need to notify the DVLA.

professional.t: The clinic asked for U&E in 1–2 weeks and BP titration; closing that loop is the practice’s responsibility.

community.t: Community pharmacist (New Medicine Service, medicines review); Stroke Association information; home BP monitoring advice.

Concern: stroke like her mother; side effects

Home BP readings seated and standing
Timing of symptoms in relation to each change

playbook.diagnosis: Symptomatic postural hypotension from an unintended losartan overdose (150 mg daily) after a dose change; possible statin-associated muscle symptoms; secondary prevention after TIA otherwise appropriate.
playbook.diagnosisLay: “Your blood pressure is dropping when you stand because you’ve been taking extra losartan by mistake. The aches may be the cholesterol tablet — a blood test will tell us more.”

management.reflectIce: “You’re worried the tablets are harming you, and you’re frightened of a stroke like your mum’s. Let’s fix what’s causing the dizziness and keep the tablets that protect you.”
management.psychosocial: Kofi to bring her tomorrow; fit note if needed; drink regularly at work.
sharedPlan: Stop the old losartan 50 mg; continue losartan 100 mg
Nurse lying/standing BP and bloods tomorrow: U&E, CK, LFT, FBC, TSH
Statin plan by CK result; consider switching if symptoms persist
Pharmacist review and one updated list or organiser
safetyNet: 999 for face, arm or speech symptoms, even if brief
Same-day contact for fainting, black stools or dark urine with weakness

pitfalls.intro: The leaflet theory tempts candidates to agree and stop something — or to dismiss her and insist on everything. The station rewards finding the mechanism.

items.fail: Never asks how she actually takes her tablets.
items.why: The duplicated losartan is the cause and is only found by asking.
items.fix: Ask her to read each box and describe her pill organiser.

items.fail: Stops the statin and losartan together “to see which it is”.
items.why: Two simultaneous changes hide the cause and remove stroke protection.
items.fix: Correct the dosing error first; check CK; change one thing at a time.

items.fail: Says “you must take them or you’ll have a stroke”.
items.why: Fear-based instruction ignores her experience and reduces adherence.
items.fix: Acknowledge the symptoms, explain the benefit, and agree a plan.

timeMap.d: Postural light-headedness; TIA, cardiac, bleeding, muscle screen; home BP seated and standing; read the boxes.
Duplicate losartan; stop the 50 mg; keep clopidogrel and statin; bloods and nurse tomorrow.

wordPics.clearFail: Agrees to stop the new medicines, or insists she keeps taking everything; no postural BP, no question about how she takes them, no stroke safety-net.
wordPics.fail: Suspects side effects and arranges bloods but misses the duplicated losartan, or makes several changes at once.
wordPics.pass: Characterises the dizziness, uses the home monitor to show a postural drop, finds the duplicated losartan, corrects it, continues antiplatelet and statin with a CK plan, arranges U&E and nurse review, and safety-nets with FAST.
wordPics.clearPass: All of the Pass, plus: links the plan to her fear of stroke, addresses fluid restriction at work, involves the pharmacist to prevent recurrence, and confirms the changes by teach-back.

avoid.instead: “You were right to notice — let’s work out which tablet and why.”
avoid.why: Validates her engagement and keeps her on board.

avoid.dont: “Stop the statin and the losartan and we’ll see.”
avoid.instead: “Let’s correct the extra losartan first and check a muscle blood test.”
avoid.why: One change at a time identifies the cause safely.

avoid.instead: “You had a cough on ramipril, so we’ll stay with losartan at the right dose.”
avoid.why: Check the allergy and intolerance record.
